_README: Data layer for the CV Generator. The app may SELECT, ORDER and OMIT text from this file. It may never compose, paraphrase or interpolate. The only fillable slots are {{COMPANY}} {{ROLE}} {{CITY}} {{DATE}} {{ECHO}} in letterBlocks. Extend this file rather than letting the app write anything. STANDING CONSTRAINT, added 14 Sept 2026: the app may never modify its own rules, thresholds, weights or severities. Data changes behaviour; a human changes data. Any feature that would let the program edit this file is out of scope permanently, not deferred - see the w-qualification entry in data.warnings for the concrete case this was written to close off.

archetypes.label: Customer operations / back office / contact centre

Its basis for THIS archetype is reliability/service-environment evidence, not relevant duties - high-volume service delivered to a fixed standard under time pressure, in a real Irish workplace, with a written reference, held alongside full-time postgraduate study with no absences across the shifts worked. That is what a back-office/operations reader is actually screening for (can this person hold a standard under pressure, show up reliably), not food service duties themselves, which are never claimed as transferable. role-dmart (Customer Service Assistant, D-Mart, Mumbai) is now RESOLVED, 17 Sept 2026, on Derin's own stated basis. Two provenance categories were separated first, because this is the point that matters more than the eventual bullets: what Derin stated himself (rotated across all the role's areas - shop-floor customer assistance, merchandising, billing/cashier, inventory/backroom, store standards and teamwork; ~10 months, Mar-Dec 2021; taken on to fund his own college tuition) is usable; everything scraped from job-board postings for that job title (specific duty bullets, a "typical shift" narrative, a skills list, anything about online order picking, cycle counts or pilferage procedures) is NOT usable, because a generic job description for a job title is not evidence of what this person did - see _sourceOfTruth. role-dmart's own basis for THIS archetype, unlike role-blarney's: direct, relevant duties - floor assistance, first-line complaints, POS and returns in a high-volume store is the closest thing on file to the job being applied for, not reliability-adjacent evidence the way Blarney is. Updated relative strengths, so role-blarney drops from customer-ops before role-dmart or role-tcs by connection to the reasoning above rather than by coincidence of priority numbers: role-dmart core (bul-dmart-floor, priority 2 - the direct-relevance bullet, never trimmed alone), role-tcs core (priority 1 throughout - see 19 Sept addendum below), role-blarney filler (not customer-facing; kept for Irish work reference, reliability alongside full-time study, and no employment gap - stays all-priority-5, the whole entry droppable first under trimPolicy.basisRule, correctly, now that it's the only one of the three with no direct-relevance claim). Derin's own basis text for role-dmart under THIS archetype, verbatim: 'Direct customer service: floor assistance, first-line complaints, POS and returns in a high-volume store. The closest thing to the job being applied for.' - unchanged from the resolution above, just restated in his own new words. Elsewhere (finance-ops, insurance-pensions, retail-parttime - any archetype including role-dmart that isn't this one), his own basis text is: 'ten months of paid people-facing work held alongside first-year study' - strength support, not core. bul-dmart-till is DELETED (Derin's own instruction, 19 Sept 2026: his content spec supplied only bul-dmart-floor, and asked, given the gap, for the till bullet to go rather than have content invented for it) - role-dmart now carries a single bullet. trimPolicy._answer: Strength (basis.strength on the group/variant itself: required > core > support > filler) replaces the old 1-5 priority integer entirely - see basisRule below for the mechanical-enforcement history. Confirmed by Derin 19 Sept 2026 (the 'A-E' six-decision-follow-up spec, part A).
order: 1. SHORTEN. Swap a block to its own `.short` text, one block at a time, re-measuring after each swap, stopping the instant the model fits. Order: strength ascending (filler, then support, then core, then required - EVERY strength is eligible here, including required and core: 'The profile is required and is the single most-shortened block in the real documents,' Derin's own words), then within a strength, by the block's current rendered height, descending. A block with no `.short` variant is simply not a candidate at this step - not an error (see the short-variant coverage reporter js/validate.js prints at load time).

2. DROP. Only once step 1 is fully exhausted (nothing left un-shortened) and the model still overflows. Drop filler bullets first, then support - NEVER core, NEVER required. Within a strength, 'last-included-first': the bullet that appears latest in the model (i.e. the one bulletBlocksFor's own JD-overlap ordering trusted least) goes first. Never drop a role/project's last remaining bullet on its own - if every remaining candidate at a strength would orphan its heading, the whole entry (heading, dates, and bullets together) is dropped as one unit instead, same last-included-first tie-break.

3. HARD FAILURE. If it still overflows after step 1 and step 2 are both fully exhausted: STOP. Do not render, do not shrink margins, do not shrink the font, and never emit a two-page document silently. Name the failure on screen, list exactly what was shortened and dropped to get there, and refuse the download - the Page-fit gate in js/verify.js's runGates() already disables the download button the moment CVPageFit.measure() still reports an overflow after the trim loop gives up; js/app.js's trim-log panel is what lists the steps.
neverDo: Shrink the margins below the values in style.page.margin
Shrink any font size below the values in style.sizes
Silently strip the CV to a skeleton to force a fit
Drop or shorten-past-zero a core or required block - shortening is allowed (in fact expected - see step 1), dropping is not
Emit a document that overflows one page without refusing the download and saying so on screen
trimPolicy.note: Trimming is a safety net, not the main mechanism. The archetype's include list is what normally decides whether Blarney and D-Mart appear at all. If trimming fires often for a given archetype, that archetype's include list is wrong - tell Derin rather than trimming every time. In three years of Derin's own real hand-built application documents, page-fit was never actually solved by deleting a section - it was always solved by shortening a sentence. That is why shortening now runs to exhaustion BEFORE anything is ever dropped, a straight reversal of this file's original (13 Sept 2026) drop-only design.
trimPolicy.basisRule: Derin, 14 Sept 2026 (REVIEW-RESPONSE-3.md section 2), verbatim: 'An item's stated basis is its trim priority. They are the same field, not two... If a section has no stated basis, it is the first thing trimmed - because nobody could say why it was there... That also kills inheritance-by-accident structurally: a new archetype cannot inherit a basis, because an empty basis field means "trim first", which is loud and visible rather than silent and wrong.' STATUS, updated 19 Sept 2026 (superseding the original entry below, kept for history, not deleted): this is now mechanically enforced, not just recorded policy. bulletVariants[gid].basis and profileVariants[i].basis are {strength, why} objects living directly on the group/variant, js/validate.js refuses to load a data file where any group or profile variant is missing one or uses an unrecognised strength, and js/trim.js's shorten-then-drop ladder reads `basis.strength` directly - there is no longer a separate numeric `priority` field that basis merely explained; basis IS the field the app executes against. ORIGINAL 14 SEPT 2026 ENTRY, preserved verbatim for history: 'Applied concretely to consulting-tech's role-blarney/vol inclusion (see that archetype's _why) - the specific gap this rule was written to close. STATUS, stated plainly rather than implied: this is a recorded policy, not (yet) a mechanically enforced one. Nothing in js/validate.js or js/trim.js currently checks that an archetype including role-blarney or vol has a non-empty _why covering them, and bulletVariants priority numbers (which is what trim.js actually reads) are not derived from _why at all - they are set independently and, for b-blarney/b-dmart, already happen to be priority 5. Applying this rule found one more live, previously-unflagged instance while writing it down: customer-ops includes role-blarney with no _why at all (see its own _pendingReview) - not resolved, since inventing a basis Derin has not stated would be exactly the guessing this project exists to prevent. A second, separate gap this rule does not close: volunteering ("vol") has no trim mechanism in js/trim.js at all - it is rendered unconditionally by buildCertificationsAndVolunteering() whenever an archetype's include list names it, with no bulletVariants-style priority and no way for trimPolicy to drop it short of manually editing excludeFactIds. So "volunteering... first to drop when tight" is not actually true in code today for any archetype, regardless of what its basis says. Queued, not built here - out of scope for what was asked (write the basis, not rebuild the trim engine).' The volunteering gap this original entry flagged is STILL open as of 19 Sept 2026 - js/trim.js's rewrite did not touch buildCertificationsAndVolunteering()/volunteering at all (out of scope for the A-E pass, which was about bulletVariants/profileVariants only); tracked as its own remaining work-order item, not silently closed by this update.

matchRule._why: ONE matcher, used by neverClaim, knownAbsentTools, skill tags, warning patterns and countHits. Four separate hand-rolled techniques is how 'aca' came to match 'vacancy'.
matchRule.syntax: A trailing * on a term means STEM (match inflections). No * means EXACT WORD.
matchRule.exact: \b{escaped}\b            - use for acronyms and short terms. 'aca' must NOT match 'academic'.
matchRule.stem: \b{escaped}\w*\b        - use for word families. 'reconcil*' catches reconcile, reconciled, reconciling, reconciliation.
matchRule.countHits: /(?=\b{escaped}(\w*)?\b)/gi - the lookahead is required, or consecutive repeats swallow each other and 'sql sql sql' counts 2.
matchRule._trap: A stem on a short term reintroduces the exact bug it was meant to fix: \baca\w*\b matches 'academic'. Never put * on a term under about six characters unless you have tested it against real ad text.
